data.why: An airplane in a green field, built as a rig: a tube with wings, wheels, a propeller and flaps that swing. It opens close on the plane rolling, and the chain is no lift, then an engine, then a runway that is too long (a gauge ticking to 300), then flaps and takeoff. The camera stays on the plane and the wing for the airfoil name, with white air flows for the myth and the real mechanism, and it ends on the plane back down with windows, a landing light and boarding stairs.

ideas.idea: bolt wings to a tube and roll it across a field and you think you have an airplane
at slow speed the wings lift nothing, so it only rolls along the grass with its weight pressing down
an engine and a propeller pull it much faster
even fast, a small plane needs hundreds of meters of runway before the wings lift it
flaps swing down so the wing lifts sooner, and the plane leaves the ground
the wing's curved shape is an airfoil
the curved top bends the air downward, so the wing is pushed up
air racing over the top to catch up with the air below is not what lifts a wing
the air on top actually gets there first, and the wing throws it down so the plane goes up
the plane comes back down and gets windows, a landing light and boarding stairs
calm: a finished airplane on the grass

chain.shows: the plane rolls along the grass with yellow weight arrows pressing down and nothing lifting
chain.stakes: the plane never leaves the ground, so it is only a rolling tube

chain.shows: a gauge beside the plane ticks up to 300 and turns red
chain.stakes: a field far too short means the plane never gets airborne

surprises.claim: A Cessna 172 needs a takeoff ground roll of roughly 300 meters (about 960 feet) at sea level at maximum weight
surprises.search: Cessna 172 takeoff ground roll 960 feet sea level

surprises.claim: Flaps let a plane lift off and land at a lower speed and in a shorter distance
surprises.search: how flaps shorten takeoff roll lower stall speed

surprises.claim: A wing lifts by deflecting air downward, which pushes the wing up (Newton's third law)
surprises.search: NASA how wings generate lift deflecting air downward

surprises.claim: Air over the top of a wing reaches the trailing edge before the air below it, so the equal transit time explanation is wrong
surprises.search: equal transit time myth wing lift air over top arrives first
